title: Implementation of Armenia's LDN commitments through sustainable land management and restoration of degraded landscapes (FAO/GEF, GCP/ARM/010/GFF)
summary: This FAO-implemented, GEF-financed project helps Armenia meet its national Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) targets. It works at national level on policy, LDN monitoring and capacity, and on the ground in two landscapes: Sisian (former Gorayk) community in Syunik and Tumanyan community in Lori, where it supports restoration of degraded grassland and cropland, forest restoration (jointly with the FAO/GCF project) and land-based value chains such as dairy, honey, berries and organic vegetables.
activities: Strengthen enabling environment: LDN integrated in policies and law, intersectoral coordination mechanism
Map land-degradation trends and drivers, set LDN baselines and targets in Lori and Syunik (Trends.Earth, Collect Earth)
Participatory integrated land-management plans in target communities and 'LDN learning landscapes'
Restore degraded grassland and cropland; forest restoration with FAO/GCF co-financing
Strengthen two land-based value chains (at least one focused on women) and update university curricula
Monitoring system for LDN indicators and UNCCD reporting
results: Planned targets (ProDoc): 4,000 ha degraded grassland restored; 7,300 ha forest land restored (co-financing); 166,000 ha under SLM (110,000 forest, 50,000 grassland, 6,000 cropland); 2,500 beneficiaries

Reported to date (UN Armenia): about 300 ha degraded arable land improved in Tumanyan and Sisian (sainfoin, alfalfa, grains); 34,000 vegetable seedlings distributed; 120 beehives, first honey harvest Aug-Sep 2024

title: ADB Strengthening Environmental Resilience and Fostering Sustainable Economy for Lake Sevan (TA 10148-ARM) and GEF 'Building Nature-Positive Future for Lake Sevan'
summary: ADB technical assistance (2023-2025) prepared climate-resilient development planning for Lake Sevan, including a spatial and zoning evaluation of the Sevan National Park recreation zone, pipeline investment scenarios for wastewater treatment in Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis, and a preliminary design of sewerage network expansion in selected Gegharkunik communities. A GEF project (concept approved March 2026) is preparing a larger ADB investment.
activities: Policy and institutional reform report, sustainable tourism potential and zoning recommendations, harmonised construction guidelines for the Sevan National Park recreational zone
Pipeline projects report on wastewater treatment and sewerage for Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis; financial sustainability analysis for decentralised sanitation
Working paper 'Resilience for Lake Sevan: Leveraging the Economic Value of Armenia's Most Vital Ecosystem'
Preliminary design of sewerage network expansion in selected Gegharkunik communities (added Dec 2024)
results: TA completed 31 Dec 2025; completion report September 2026

title: Fueling Green Recovery in Armenia - advancing forest infrastructure and creating sustainable jobs for rural communities (GCF SAP059)
summary: EPIU implements a five-year Green Climate Fund project to expand national forest-seedling infrastructure and plant new forest in eight marzes that are not covered by the FAO/GCF forest resilience project. It aims to supply 20 million seedlings a year by 2030, establish about 1,300 ha of forest in mountain areas and create about 3,500 green jobs for vulnerable rural people. Hayantar SNCO, Armenia Tree Project and My Forest Armenia are the implementing partners named in the funding proposal.
activities: Seed bank and greenhouses under Hayantar SNCO (one 1,000 m2 greenhouse in each beneficiary marz), plus greenhouses at Armenia Tree Project and My Forest Armenia
About 1,000 household backyard seedling nurseries in vulnerable municipalities
Establishment of around 1,300 ha of forest (about 4 million trees) on 120 mapped plots of 3-40 ha in about 50 municipalities
Non-timber forest product value chains and agroforestry; 3,500 sustainable jobs target
Digital monitoring (MRV) and investment platform for forest restoration

title: ADB Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project (Loan 2363-ARM) and Additional Financing (Loan 2860-ARM)
summary: Two ADB loans rehabilitated water supply and some sanitation systems of small towns and villages served by the Armenia Water and Sewerage Company outside Yerevan, improving water supply hours and metering. ADB reports 21 small towns and 97 villages rehabilitated; the Additional Financing subprojects included Echmiadzin and nearby villages, Talin, Noyemberyan and Kapan.
activities: Rehabilitation of water supply networks, pumping and storage in small towns and villages under AWSC
Additional Financing subprojects: Echmiadzin town with villages of Armavir and Aragatsotn marzes; Talin town; Noyemberyan town; Kapan town and Achanan village (Syunik)
Institutional support to AWSC and metering
results: Average water supply rose from 6 to 14 hours a day; bill payment rose from 48 to 90 percent; metered connections from 40 to 77 percent (ADB results page)
More than 600,000 people benefited, about a quarter poor (ADB results page)

title: Natural Resources Management and Poverty Reduction Project (World Bank P057847 + GEF P069917)
summary: World Bank IDA project with a GEF biodiversity component to arrest natural-resource degradation and reduce rural poverty in the upper watersheds of northern Armenia. It worked in micro-catchments in Tavush and Gegharkunik marzes (community forest plans, pasture management, small grants) and supported management of Dilijan State Reserve and Lake Sevan National Park.
activities: Community forest management plans, pasture management and small grants in selected micro-catchments
Rehabilitation and sustainable management of state forests; forest sector institutional and legal framework
Management of Dilijan State Reserve and Lake Sevan National Park; capacity of the Department of Bio-resources and Land Protection
results: Community forest management plans developed for five Noyemberyan-area communities in 2006-2009; 40 ha of degraded forest regenerated in Koghb and Jujevan (by REC Caucasus) - per UNDP 5353 ProDoc

title: Biodiversity and sustainable local development in Armenia (BMZ/KfW)
summary: Germany's largest nature-protection grant to Armenia funds the Ministry of Environment to strengthen management of selected nature reserves and protected forests, improve forest management by local forest authorities, expand and adjust protected-area boundaries, and support income opportunities in communities bordering protected areas. Main implementation started in July 2024 and runs about six years.
activities: Equipment, infrastructure, planning and management tools for prioritised nature reserves and protected forests
Adjust cadastral boundaries of protected areas, expand them and add new areas
Strengthen local forest authorities for sustainable forest management and carbon storage
Ecotourism and revenue generation for protected-area administrations
Community development near protected areas, e.g. a financial participatory approach in communities adjacent to Lake Arpi National Park (2026)

title: Livestock Development in Armenia / Creating markets for Armenian livestock farmers (SDC, implemented by SDA)
summary: The project improved milk and meat value chains for smallholder farmers in about 220 rural settlements, starting in Syunik and Vayots Dzor and extending to Gegharkunik, Tavush, Lori and Shirak. It built private veterinary and artificial insemination service points and linked farmers to collectors and processors.
activities: Veterinary and artificial insemination service network
Links between farmers, milk collection and processors; cross-border trade with Georgia
Extension and training, electronic animal register
results: 102 veterinary and 52 artificial insemination points established 2014-2021 in six marzes
Services reached over 15,200 households in 217 rural settlements in 2020; total milk production up 78 percent 2014-2020 in the northern marzes (project data as reported)
46,450 farmers earned more income; 396 off-farm jobs created

title: Swiss Humanitarian Aid: Armenia early recovery after floods 2024 (Lori and Tavush)
summary: After the May 2024 floods in northern Armenia, Swiss Humanitarian Aid experts assessed damaged bridges, designed three pedestrian footbridges, trained Armenian engineers in hydraulic engineering and resilient infrastructure, and produced an event analysis of the floods in Lori and Tavush.
activities: Technical assessment of damaged bridges and infrastructure; design of three footbridges at Saratovka, Alaverdi and Ayrum
Hydraulic engineering training for engineers of the Roads Department, Civil Protection, Water Resources Management Agency and universities
Event analysis of the 2024 floods with the Crisis Management State Academy, Armhydromet and the Swiss FOEN
results: Event analysis found water flow exceeded infrastructure capacity; recommendation to define hydraulic parameters before rebuilding (SDC, July 2025)

title: Water and Agriculture Integrated Development for Armenia (WAIDA / PADISEAA) - AFD and EU
summary: An AFD/EU programme with two pillars: nationwide water-sector support co-financing the World Bank WISE program (excluding Syunik), and a Syunik-only pillar (LITDS) to restore and modernise irrigation, improve access to water and develop agricultural value chains. The EU page lists the programme as ongoing from April 2026 to March 2034.
activities: Pillar 1 (WISE, nationwide excluding Syunik): institutional support to the Water Committee/WSA, technical assistance and grants for Water User Associations, rehabilitation of strategic water infrastructure

Pillar 2 (LITDS, Syunik): rehabilitation and modernisation of irrigation systems (gravity-fed networks, pumping stations, water reuse), climate-resilient agriculture, agribusiness and extension services
Land management support

title: RESILAND: Armenia Resilient Landscapes Project (World Bank P179988 / GEF 11046)
summary: The World Bank-supported RESILAND project, executed by EPIU, restores fragmented forests, degraded wetlands and abandoned mining sites in four marzes and builds the policy and institutional framework for landscape management. It also supports community forestry, non-timber forest products and ecotourism as alternative incomes. The GEF-side documentation targets improved land condition on 25,800 ha.
activities: Policy review and institutional capacity for integrated landscape management
Landscape restoration: forest restoration (rebuilding fragmented forests), wetland restoration and mining-site restoration
Community benefits: community-based forestry management and ecotourism development
Project management, monitoring, evaluation and communication

title: Rehabilitation of the Arpa-Sevan tunnel (Abu Dhabi Fund for Development support)
summary: Rehabilitation of the Arpa-Sevan tunnel, a 48 km conduit that diverts the Arpa and Yeghegis rivers into Lake Sevan to stabilise and raise the lake level. Works supported by the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development ran from 2010 (including lining and flume replacement in Tunnel No. 2 from the Yeghegis site); the Water Committee continues emergency-section works.
activities: Reconstruction of deformed stretches of tunnel lining; replacement of the concrete flume in Tunnel No. 2 from the Yeghegis site
2024-2025: 245 m of lining rehabilitated, tunnel capacity raised to 20 m3/s; next emergency sections planned from September 2026 (AMD 2.082 billion)
results: Tunnel capacity raised to 20 m3/s after 2024-2025 works (Water Committee)

title: UNDP Improving water reservoir management capabilities of Armenia for resilience to climate risks
summary: UNDP project supporting modernisation of Armenia's reservoir management and the resilience of downstream communities: dam safety, hydrological and flow monitoring, early warning and emergency preparedness, and renewable energy at reservoirs. UNDP coverage names the Aparan, Azat and Metsavan reservoirs.
activities: Modern hydrometeorological monitoring systems and solar power at the Aparan, Azat and Metsavan reservoirs
Warning sirens and engineering-geological and geophysical studies at the Azat reservoir
GIS-based hazard and inundation maps for downstream populations; scenario-based simulation exercise (workshop March 2026 with local administrations in Aparan, Ashtarak, Tashir and Masis)

title: Enhancing Livelihoods in Rural Communities of Armenia through Mainstreaming and Strengthening Agricultural Biodiversity Conservation and Utilization (UNEP/GEF 5483)
summary: UNEP/GEF medium-size project executed by the Ministry of Nature Protection, the Armenian National Agrarian University and Bioversity International. It aimed to conserve agricultural biodiversity (notably local fruit tree varieties and crop wild relatives) and build a sustainable basis for using it to improve rural livelihoods.
activities: National capacity and institutional framework for agricultural biodiversity management
Community-level agrobiodiversity conservation and use in pilot locations (final locations not confirmed)
Market and value-chain support for biodiversity-friendly products

title: Social Investment and Local Development Project (SILD) and Additional Financing
summary: SILD finances community-driven microprojects in vulnerable communities and larger intercommunity subprojects (schools, kindergartens, water supply, sanitation, community centres, health facilities, minor irrigation). The 2020 additional financing was to support 55 communities.
activities: Microprojects selected by community vulnerability ranking and socio-economic impact
Intercommunity subprojects
Institutional strengthening of ATDF
results: Original project completed 98 microprojects and 52 subprojects (closed 2022)
Additional financing: 15 of 17 microprojects completed and all 38 subprojects by late 2024; project closed 31 May 2025

title: LEAD4Shirak - Local Empowerment of Actors for Development of Shirak region
summary: LEAD4Shirak introduced the EU LEADER approach in Shirak marz through two Local Action Groups that prepared local development strategies and funded local initiatives. It closed in March 2026 after supporting 48 businesses and 84 community initiatives.
activities: Regulatory framework and delivery system for community-led local development (CLLD/LEADER)
Two Local Action Groups with multi-annual local development strategies
Grant scheme for local economic and social initiatives
results: 48 businesses and 84 community initiatives supported; 117 new jobs (EU, Mar 2026)

title: Enhancing the land-based adaptation of communities adjacent to arid zones and forest protected areas of Armenia (Adaptation Fund, EPIU)
summary: Follow-on Adaptation Fund project executed by EPIU with the Dilijan National Park and Khosrov Forest State Reserve SNCOs. It aims to duplicate and expand the mechanisms of the previous project (Khosrov-Dilijan) for communities adjacent to arid zones and forest protected areas; a search summary adds pasture and irrigation rehabilitation, solar systems, greenhouses and farmer training.
activities: Duplicate and expand land-based adaptation mechanisms of the previous Adaptation Fund project

title: Communal Infrastructure Programme (CIP) II, phases 1-3, with EU NIF contribution
summary: CIP rehabilitates water supply and sewerage in the service areas of regional utilities (Shirak, Lori, Nor Akunq, AWSC) to give 24-hour water supply, and the EU contribution adds a wastewater treatment plant in Armavir and a pilot in 560 villages outside utility areas.
activities: Rehabilitation of water supply networks and urgent sewer measures in utility areas (phase 3: Shirak, Lori, Nor Akunq, AWSC)
Wastewater treatment plant in Armavir (EU NIF)
Pilot in 560 villages not assigned to water utilities (EU NIF)

title: Digital Technologies in support of Agriculture Value Chains and Rural Development (vineyard registry)
summary: FAO supported the Ministry of Economy in designing and launching a national digital Vineyard Register System and a farmer mobile application, and organised a 2025 study tour to Georgia on grapevine nurseries and vineyard data systems.
activities: Vineyard Register System (national digital platform for vineyard oversight, certification and planning)
Requirements for a mobile app for farmers in the grape value chain
Capacity building for use of the registry

title: ADB Sustainable Water Use Assessment for Productivity Enhancement (ARM-SWAP)
summary: Small ADB technical assistance (approved December 2024) assessing whether water discharged from aquaculture can be reused for irrigation in the Ararat Valley: water accounting, productivity, technical feasibility, governance and sustainability.
activities: Water accounting and productivity assessment; feasibility of reusing discharged aquaculture water for irrigation
Governance framework and socio-economic and environmental sustainability review

title: Innovative Agriculture Training and Learning Camp (AGRI CAMP)
summary: AGRI CAMP renovates facilities at the Armenian National Agrarian University so rural entrepreneurs can learn new production and business skills. Funding added in 2021 supports agricultural cooperatives and women's access to agricultural innovation.
activities: Renovation of training facilities at the Armenian National Agrarian University
Strengthening formal agricultural cooperatives and business development
Skills and networks for female agripreneurs

title: Resilience and Economic Recovery of Border Communities in Armenia (REBCA)
summary: REBCA combined humanitarian cash support with livelihood and economic recovery in 15 border settlements hit by the September 2022 escalation. It reached more than 1,000 households in the enlarged communities of Vardenis, Sisian and Jermuk.
activities: Cash assistance and social work support
Support to agricultural activities and (self-)employment
Resource and capacity development of local communities

title: Integrated multi-level capacity building for climate-adapted rural agriculture in Tavush, Shirak and Lori Marz
summary: A BMZ-funded civil-society project on capacity building for climate-adapted rural agriculture in the northern marzes of Tavush, Shirak and Lori, implemented by the German NGO Hoffnungszeichen. No further description or community list could be found.

title: Enhancing capacity for climate action in Armenian agri-food systems
summary: Small FAO facility project to help Armenia access global climate and environmental finance and to build capacity of agricultural communities in climate-smart agriculture. No project page or sites were found.
